To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the titanium complex prepared from the reaction of TiCl3 and 18-crown ether catalyzes the hydroboration of unsaturated compounds with NaBH4 to produce sodium organoboranes with high regioselectivity and stereoselectivity.
the titanium complex promotes the hydroboration of various unsaturated compounds with high regio-and stereo-selectivities.

the titanium complex prepared from titanium(III) chloride and sodium borohydride in THF in presence of 18- crown-6 promotes the regio- and stereoselective hydroboration of various unsaturated compounds with sodium borohydrid, giving the corresponding sodium organoboranes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of novel titanium catalysts for hydroboration of various unsaturated compounds.
the development of new synthetic methodologies and the study of the reaction mechanisms of organometallic compounds.
the development of new synthetic methodologies based on transition metals, particularly titanium, in organic synthesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the regioselectivity is determined by steric factors, and the stereoselectivity is governed by the nature of the double bond.

the regio- and stereoselectivities of the catalytic hydroborations depend on the steric and electronic properties of the substituents of the unsaturated substrates and the steric and coordinational properties of the catalyst.
the hydroboration of alkenes and alkadienes with NaBH4 in the presence of the titanium complex is regio- and stereoselective.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this catalytic reaction is highly regio- and stereoselective, and that this reaction can be used to synthesize optically active alcohols with high optical purity from optically active olefins.

the titanium complex catalyzes the hydroboration of various unsaturated substrates with high selectivity and that the selectivities are determined by the steric effect of the substituents on the unsaturated substrates.

the regioselectivity of the hydroboration of alkenes is controlled by the steric bulk of the substituents at the double bonds, and the stereo-selectivity of the hydroborations of alkenes, 1,3-dienes and unsaturated ethers is controlled by the substituents of the titanium complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regioselectivity of the reaction depends on the nature of the double bond.
the titanium complex catalyzes the regio- and stereoselective hydroboration of various carbon–carbon double bond systems.
the regio- and stereoselectivity of the reaction depends on the structure of the substrate.
